title: Annotatio V §.II: Picherellus summons Augustine — two things in the sacrament, diverse modes of eating
pass_a_gloss: In the name of this whole matter a certain pontifical yet sober and moderate Author often cited, Petrus Picherellus, introduces Augustine in summary — whose words it will be welcome to no one not to have reviewed here; so indeed he, Opusc. Theol. p. 176 at the end through p. 178 in the middle: Augustine certainly, he says, understanding those two things in the Supper’s sacrament, makes diverse modes of eating it, and from the Lord’s words in the Gospel according to Matthew and in many other places explains them everywhere by antithesis.
pass_b_english: For this whole point the sober pontifical author Petrus Picherellus (often cited) brings Augustine in summary — Opusc. Theol. pp. 176–178.
Augustine, seeing two things in the Supper’s sacrament, makes diverse modes of eating and explains them by antithesis across Matthew and many other places.
source_text: Totius hujus nomine, Augustinum in compendio introducit pontificius quidam, ast sobrius Autor moderatusque, sæpius citatus Petrus Picherellus, cujus verba hîc recensuisse nemini ingratum accidere poterit; ita verò ille, Opusc. Theol. p. 176. in fine usque ad p. 178. in med. Augustinus profecto, ait, duas illas res in Cœnæ sacramento intelligens, diversos illius manducandi modos facit, de verbis Domini in Evangelium secundum Matth. & multis aliis locis, passim per antithesin explicat.
